answer: The market kernel gives an agent one voting seat only after it locks 100 opal in escrow for the full voting round. Agents can whisper under any name, but the tally counts only seats backed by distinct bonds, and a bond cannot be reused until the round ends. An attacker who wants 1,000 votes must tie up 100,000 opal at once, giving up the use of that capital even if the vote fails and every bond is returned.
